wizard.title: How to play {game}
wizard.wiezen.1.title: The goal
wizard.wiezen.1.body: Four players, each on their own. Every deal you get 13 cards. First you promise how many tricks you will take (that is the bidding), then you try to make good on it. Make your promise and you win points from the others.
wizard.wiezen.2.title: Cards and trump
wizard.wiezen.2.body: Ace is the highest card, then king, queen, jack, ten … down to the two. The last card dealt is turned face up: that suit is trump. A trump card always beats a plain card.
wizard.wiezen.3.title: Bidding
wizard.wiezen.3.body: You choose what you promise. 'Ask & join' means: I want a partner and together we take 8 tricks. If nobody joins you may play alone (5 tricks). Stronger hands bid higher: abondance (9 or more tricks alone) or misère (not a single trick). Hold exactly three aces and you must call troel: the player with the fourth ace becomes your partner, leads that ace, and its suit is trump.
wizard.wiezen.4.title: Playing tricks
wizard.wiezen.4.body: The leader plays a card; the others follow clockwise. You must follow suit if you can. If you cannot, you are free to trump or throw something away. The highest trump wins the trick, otherwise the highest card of the suit led. The winner leads the next trick.
wizard.wiezen.5.title: Scoring
wizard.wiezen.5.body: Make your contract and the opponents pay you; miss it and you pay them. Every trick above your target earns extra, every trick short costs you. The app does all the maths — you get a summary after each deal.
wizard.manille.1.title: The goal
wizard.manille.1.body: Manille is played in two fixed teams: you and the player opposite you are partners. Together you collect card points. Take more than half and your team wins the deal.
wizard.manille.2.title: The ten rules
wizard.manille.2.body: Careful: here the ten (the 'manille') is the highest card, above the ace. The order is 10, ace, king, queen, jack, 9, 8, 7. The ten is worth 5 points, the ace 4, the king 3, the queen 2 and the jack 1 — 60 points in total.
wizard.manille.3.title: Trump and the duty to trump
wizard.manille.3.body: The dealer picks the trump suit. You must follow suit. If you cannot, you must trump — and if you can overtrump, you must. Only when you have no trump left may you discard.
wizard.manille.4.title: Scoring
wizard.manille.4.body: After eight tricks you count each team's card points. The team above 30 wins the deal and scores the difference with 30. At 30-30 nobody scores. First team to 101 points wins the session.
wizard.bieden.1.title: The goal
wizard.bieden.1.body: Bieden is played in two fixed teams. You promise a number of points (at least 100) and try to collect them with your partner. There are 151 points in play.
wizard.bieden.2.title: Card values
wizard.bieden.2.body: In the trump suit the jack is the highest card (20 points), then the nine (14), ace (11), ten (10), king (3) and queen (2). In the other suits the ace leads (11), then ten (10), king (3), queen (2), jack (1). The last trick is worth 10 extra points.
wizard.bieden.3.title: Bidding and trump
wizard.bieden.3.body: Each player gets one chance to bid or pass; raises go in steps of ten. The highest bidder leads — and the suit of that first card immediately becomes trump. What makes this game special: you may always trump, even when you could follow suit.
wizard.bieden.4.title: Scoring
wizard.bieden.4.body: If your team collects at least the points you bid, you score that bid. If you fall short, the amount goes to the opponents instead. First team to 500 points wins.
coach.tip.troel: Someone holds three aces, so troel is compulsory. The player with the fourth ace is automatically the partner and leads — that first card sets the trump.
coach.tip.joinYes: Your hand is strong enough to join: together you need 8 tricks.
coach.tip.joinNo: Joining is risky with this hand — 8 tricks together is a lot to ask. Passing is always allowed.
coach.tip.askStrong: Strong hand ({hp} honour points, {trumps} trumps). Asking is worth considering: you look for a partner for 8 tricks together.
coach.tip.askWeak: Weak hand ({hp} honour points). Passing is usually wisest — waiting costs you nothing.
coach.tip.alone: Nobody joined. Playing alone means taking 5 tricks on your own. In doubt? Better to pass.
coach.tip.chooseTrump: Pick the suit where you hold the most and the highest cards — that becomes your trump.
coach.tip.lead: You lead. A high card in your longest suit is usually a safe start.
coach.tip.leadSetsTrump: You lead and your first card sets the trump. So pick the suit you are strongest in.
coach.tip.mustFollow: You must follow suit — only those cards are clickable now.
coach.tip.cannotFollow: You do not hold the suit led. You are free to choose: trump to take the trick, or discard a card you do not need.
coach.tip.manilleTrump: You deal and pick the trump. Take the suit you hold most of — ideally with the ten or the ace in it.
coach.tip.manilleLead: You lead. Remember: the ten is the highest card here and worth 5 points.
coach.tip.manilleMustTrump: You cannot follow suit, so you must trump (and overtrump if you can).
coach.tip.biedenBidYes: Strong hand ({hp} honour points). A bid of 100 or more is defensible — remember your partner collects points too.
coach.tip.biedenBidNo: Rather weak hand ({hp} honour points). Passing costs nothing; let the opponents take the risk.
coach.tip.biedenLeadSetsTrump: You bid highest, so you lead — and that first card sets the trump.
coach.tip.biedenFollowOrTrump: In bieden you may always trump, even when you could follow suit. Pick whatever pays best.

guide.title: Rules & explanation
guide.intro: Pick a topic. Every chapter walks you through the rules step by step — you can always go back.
guide.readMore: All the rules of this game
guide.basis.title: The basics
guide.basis.summary: What every game in this app has in common: the table, the cards and the trick.
guide.basis.tafel.title: Four players around a table
guide.basis.tafel.body: Every game here is played by four. You sit across from one player and next to two others. Dealing, bidding and playing all go clockwise. The dealer moves on each round, so everyone gets an equal turn at leading.
guide.basis.kaarten.title: The cards
guide.basis.kaarten.body: Wiezen uses the full 52-card pack: everyone gets 13. Manillen and bieden use a short 32-card pack (twos through sixes are removed): everyone gets 8. The ace is usually the highest card, then king (K), queen (Q), jack (J), ten, nine … down to the two.
guide.basis.slag.title: Winning a trick
guide.basis.slag.body: One player leads: they put down a card. The other three then play one card each, clockwise. Those four cards together are a trick. You must follow the suit that was led as long as you still hold it. The highest card in that suit wins — unless someone trumps. Whoever wins the trick leads the next one.
guide.basis.troef.title: What trumps do
guide.basis.troef.body: One suit is trump for the round. Any trump beats any card of another suit, however high: the two of trumps beats the ace of another suit. If several trumps land in one trick, the highest trump wins. How the trump suit gets decided differs per game — that is exactly what separates plain wiezen from kleurenwiezen.
guide.gewoon-wiezen.title: Plain wiezen
guide.gewoon-wiezen.summary: The classic form: the turned last card sets the trump suit.
guide.gewoon-wiezen.troef.title: The trump is face up
guide.gewoon-wiezen.troef.body: After dealing, the last card — the dealer's — is turned face up on the table. That suit is trump for the round. So everyone knows the trump suit before any bidding happens, and you can see at once how many trumps you hold yourself. That is the main information your bid rests on.
guide.gewoon-wiezen.bieden.title: The bidding round
guide.gewoon-wiezen.bieden.body: Bidding starts left of the dealer and goes clockwise. You say what you promise to take, or you pass. Any new bid must sit higher on the ladder than the bid already on the table. Once you have passed you are out. If everybody passes, the cards go back in and the next player deals again — no score.
guide.gewoon-wiezen.vraag.title: Ask & join
guide.gewoon-wiezen.vraag.body: The lowest and most common contract. You say 'I ask': I am looking for a partner. A player after you can 'join'. Together you then need at least 8 of the 13 tricks. Manage it and you both collect points from both opponents; every trick above 8 pays extra. Take 7 or fewer and you pay instead.
guide.gewoon-wiezen.alleen.title: Going alone
guide.gewoon-wiezen.alleen.body: If nobody joins, you face a choice: pass after all, or play alone. Alone means you against three, and you need at least 5 tricks. It pays more than ask & join, but you get no help. Fail and you pay all three opponents.
guide.gewoon-wiezen.troel.title: Troel
guide.gewoon-wiezen.troel.body: Hold exactly three aces and you must call 'troel' — it is not a choice. The player with the fourth ace automatically becomes your partner, even though they do not know it yet. They lead, and they are meant to lead that very ace: its suit becomes trump. Lead anything else and that card's suit becomes trump instead, but you need one more trick — 9 rather than 8. If the caller holds all four aces, the king of hearts holder is the partner and the same rule applies to that king. Troel counts double: both the win and the loss weigh more than an ordinary ask.
guide.gewoon-wiezen.hoog.title: The high contracts
guide.gewoon-wiezen.hoog.body: When you are very strong — or very weak — you bid higher. Abondance: you play alone, choose the trump suit yourself and promise 9, 10, 11 or 12 tricks. Misère: you promise to take no trick at all — one trick and you are out. Open misère is the same, with your cards face up. Solo (all 13 with trumps) and soloslim (all 13 without) sit at the top.
guide.gewoon-wiezen.punten.title: Scoring
guide.gewoon-wiezen.punten.body: Every contract has a fixed value: ask & join 2, alone 3, troel 4, abondance 6 to 9, misère 7, open misère 14, solo 20, soloslim 30. Make your contract and you collect that from each opponent; miss it and you pay the same. For ask, alone and troel the tricks above or below your target count too. It all sums to zero: what one wins, the others lose.
guide.kleurenwiezen.title: Kleurenwiezen
guide.kleurenwiezen.summary: Same rules, but whoever asks names the trump suit themselves.
guide.kleurenwiezen.verschil.title: The only difference
guide.kleurenwiezen.verschil.body: Kleurenwiezen is plain wiezen with one difference: no card is turned up. So the trump suit is not fixed when bidding starts. Every other rule — the ladder, the scores, troel, misère, abondance, following suit — is identical. If you know plain wiezen, you know this too.
guide.kleurenwiezen.vragen.title: Asking in a suit
guide.kleurenwiezen.vragen.body: Whoever asks says which suit in the same breath: 'I ask in hearts'. That suit is trump for the whole round. So you choose yourself — and naturally you choose the suit you are strongest in. If nobody joins and you play alone, your announced suit stays trump; you cannot switch any more.
guide.kleurenwiezen.meegaan.title: What that means for joining
guide.kleurenwiezen.meegaan.body: In plain wiezen you know the trump suit before bidding. Here you hear it only when someone asks — and that instantly tells you something about their hand: they are strong in that suit. So reassess your own hand the moment the suit is named. Three high cards in that suit make joining attractive; none at all and passing is the obvious call. Higher contracts are unchanged: an abondance player still picks their suit after the bidding.
guide.manillen.title: Manillen
guide.manillen.summary: Fixed teams, 32 cards, and the ten is the highest card.
guide.manillen.ploegen.title: Fixed teams
guide.manillen.ploegen.body: Unlike wiezen the partners do not change: you and the player across from you are one team for the whole match. You play with 32 cards, 8 each. You collect card points rather than tricks — what is inside the tricks is what counts.
guide.manillen.rangorde.title: The ten rules
guide.manillen.rangorde.body: Here is the surprise: the ten — the 'manille' — is the highest card, above the ace. The order is 10, A, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7. Only those top five score: ten 5, ace 4, king 3, queen 2, jack 1. Nine, eight and seven are worth nothing but can still win a trick.
guide.manillen.troefplicht.title: Follow and trump
guide.manillen.troefplicht.body: The dealer picks the trump suit. You must follow the suit led, just as in wiezen. But if you cannot, here you must trump — and if a trump is already down, you must overtrump when you can. Only a player with no trumps left may discard. That sharpens the game: you cannot hoard your trumps.
guide.manillen.punten.title: Scoring
guide.manillen.punten.body: There are 60 points in the pack. After the eight tricks each team counts its card points. The team over 30 wins the round and writes down the difference from 30: take 38 and you score 8. At 30-30 nobody scores. The first team to 101 points wins the match.
guide.bieden.title: Bieden
guide.bieden.summary: A team game where you promise points — and the trump falls with the first card.
guide.bieden.ploegen.title: Teams and target
guide.bieden.ploegen.body: Here too you and the player opposite form a fixed team, with 32 cards and 8 each. You promise points rather than tricks: at least 100 of the 151 in the pack. Reach them with your partner and you write down your bid; fall short and the amount goes to the opposition.
guide.bieden.waarden.title: Card values
guide.bieden.waarden.body: Values depend on the suit. In trumps the jack is by far the highest card (20 points), then the nine (14), the ace (11), the ten (10), the king (3) and the queen (2). In the other suits the usual order holds: ace 11, ten 10, king 3, queen 2, jack 1. The last trick of the round is worth 10 extra — 151 in total.
guide.bieden.veiling.title: The auction and the trump
guide.bieden.veiling.body: Every player gets one chance: bid or pass. Bids go up in tens, starting at 100. The highest bidder leads — and the suit of that very first card becomes trump. So you commit to your trump with your opening move, in full view of everyone.
guide.bieden.punten.title: Free trumping and scoring
guide.bieden.punten.body: The quirk of bieden: you may always trump, even when you could still follow suit. That makes every trick unpredictable. At the end each team counts its points; if the bidding team reaches its bid it writes that bid down, otherwise the opposition gets it. First team to 500 wins.
guide.scorebord.title: The scoreboard
guide.scorebord.summary: For when you are at the table with real cards and only want the score kept.
guide.scorebord.waarvoor.title: What it is for
guide.scorebord.waarvoor.body: The scoreboard plays nothing: it counts. You are at the table with friends and a real pack of cards, and the app keeps the score. You enter two to four names, optionally a target score, and add the points after every round. The standings survive closing the app.
guide.scorebord.manueel.title: Manual mode
guide.scorebord.manueel.body: In manual mode you simply type the points each player took that round — for any game at all. Handy for a game the app does not know, or when you use your own scoring. You can delete a round if you slip up, and choose whether the highest or the lowest score wins.
guide.scorebord.auto.title: Wiezen automatically
guide.scorebord.auto.body: Playing wiezen? Pick the auto mode: you indicate which contract was played (troel included), who played it, who their partner was — or that they went alone — and how many tricks were taken. The app works out the points for all four players with the same rules as the game itself, overtricks and undertricks included. No more arguments at the table.
